rules.statement: In a test project, don't report the null-forgiving operator when it is `null!` (or `[null!]`) used to pass a deliberate null argument or null entry to the code under test in an argument-validation test.
rules.why: The C# conventions make this the one exception to the ban on the `!` operator: tests have to pass a deliberate null to check null-argument validation.
rules.check: Before reporting a `!` in test code, check whether it is `null!` passed directly as an argument or collection entry to the method or constructor under test in a test that asserts it rejects null. If so, don't report it. Any other `!` in tests is still a violation.

rules.statement: When two components carry near-identical logic, such as reading a protocol parameter, applying its default and looking it up in a catalog, move it into one shared helper or extension method on the shared abstraction and call it from both.
rules.why: If each component keeps its own copy, the copies can drift apart and the components could resolve the same input differently.
rules.check: Look for private methods in different classes of the diff that repeat the same read, default and lookup steps. Flag them and ask for one shared helper or extension.
